images.rightsLabel: Free to use — Smithsonian American Art Museum
images.alt: George Catlin painting of a mounted hunter pursuing a buffalo herd across a grassy landscape bordered by trees, titled Caddo Indians Chasing Buffalo, Cross Timbers, Texas.
images.scope: George Catlin’s historical painting, dated 1846–1848 by the Smithsonian American Art Museum, depicts a mounted hunter and buffalo in the Cross Timbers of Texas. The item record names Caddo people, credits the painter and the Harrison gift, and explicitly marks the image Free to use. This is an outside artistic depiction, not a Caddo-made work, a photograph, or a survey of territory. The museum’s historical Catlin quotation is not adopted as factual synthesis. The complete available 2600×1873 digital frame and primary item/rights record were inspected; the web image is proportionally resized/recompressed, with no generated content or retouching. Cards and backdrops use CSS crops/overlays; the opened profile also shows the complete frame. This visual review adds no substantive source checks.

images.title: Cypress knees in Big Thicket National Preserve, Texas
images.credit: NPS Photo / Scott Sharaga. Big Thicket National Preserve, U.S. National Park Service.
images.creator: Scott Sharaga, National Park Service
images.rightsLabel: Public domain in the United States — NPS work
images.scope: Modern Big Thicket landscape, credited on the actual NPS page as NPS Photo / Scott Sharaga. The Tribe’s own history locates the Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas in this region, while distinguishing the two peoples before their westward migration. The image illustrates regional environmental context; it does not show a reservation boundary, an identified cultural site, or every Alabama community. The NPS ownership policy identifies agency-created material as generally public domain unless otherwise indicated; this image has an explicit agency credit and no contrary notice. The complete 6960×2499 available source frame was visually inspected. Its primary JPEG frame is proportionally resized/recompressed to 1800×646; no content is generated, retouched or added. Cards and background copies use CSS crops/overlays. No source-count increase is claimed.
